Contraception Question

By: Marion Edmunds | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We show how standard government-issue contraception may need to be rethought following a BMJ study published last year

Unique Selling Point:
We have access to individuals in the medical world who are reacting to new information in the way of a study which may change the approach to a contraceptive drug globally, in particular in low income countries. The studies highlight a possible link between the three month injection Depo-Provera, which is made of the synthetic hormone, MPA, and devastating brain tumours. This new information, while not conclusive, could have direct impact on the lives of millions of women who rely on discreet contraception to manage family planning in poorer settings. The case studies we interviewed who were suffering from meningiomas and had been on Depo-Provera for a length of time - sometimes decades - are sufficiently angry to start planning for a class action against the manufacturer of the drug, Pfizer. Their health, independence and livelihoods have been severely impacted by the Meningiomas and they are angry about the suffering they have experienced. This association has direct consequences for contraception across the developing world.

Press Release:


The Contraception Question
Dizziness, blurry vision, seizures and intense headaches. The true horror of sphenoid wing meningiomas appears to be only fully grasped by the people who have them growing inside their skulls, and the surgeons who try to help them. These invasive tumours often grow undetected for years, causing huge damage to the eyes and brain. In an investigation spanning two continents, Carte Blanche meets some of the meningioma patients who have had to undergo complex brain surgery to save their lives. Not only do they share this grisly experience, but they’ve also discovered that they were all on one of the world’s most widely available contraceptive injections - Depo-Provera - for decades. Now, new scientific evidence is suggesting a possible link between medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) - the synthetic hormone in Depo-Provera - and the development of brain tumours. Lawyers are preparing cases against the manufacturers of the so-called “jab” in several countries, including South Africa, after nine women with meningiomas approached them to consider action. Responding to growing pressure on this issue, the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) has recently recommended updating safety warnings about MPA-containing products to include the potential risk of meningioma. But for the women we have spoken to, this comes too little too late.
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Erin Bates

Script:


(VO1) IN CAPE TOWN, SCORES OF WOMEN ARE ON A WAITING LIST FOR HIGH-RISK BRAIN SURGERY.
MANY MORE HAVE ALREADY HAD THIS OPERATION, AFTER BEING DIAGNOSED WITH TUMOURS THAT GROW UNDETECTED FOR YEARS
AND CAUSE DAMAGE INSIDE THEIR SKULLS.

CAROLINE MURRAY
Meningioma Survivor, Fish Hoek
They are quite large, usually. And they sort of infiltrate into the base of the skull. So it's like a spider.

SHENE GURLING
Meningioma Survivor, Mitchell’s Plain.
I can't remember my wedding day. I can't remember the birth of my children.

WASELA ROSS
Meningioma Survivor, Ottery
When you go through that, you feel like half a life has been taken away.


LYNN JANSEN VAN RENSBURG UPSOUND: If I don’t have this invasive surgery…

(VO2 ) THIS IS A STORY TOLD TO US BY A DOZEN WOMEN ACROSS SOUTH AFRICA, WHO HAVE ALL SUFFERED FROM BRAIN TUMOURS.
IT’S PIECED TOGETHER FROM HIGH RESOLUTION SCANS, PHOTOS, BLURRY ZOOM CALLS AND FRAGMENTED MEMORIES.

BELINDA POTGIETER
Meningioma Patient, Vereeniging
It literally felt as though my brain was leaking through my ears.

ILSE SLOANE
Meningioma Patient, Somerset West
And the words wouldn't come out of my mouth correctly. It was like talking gibberish…

(VO3) BUT TOGETHER, THESE STORIES MAKE A COLLECTIVE PICTURE OF PAIN, SUFFERING AND DEVASTATING LOSS.

HENTHA SWANEPOEL
Meningioma Survivor, Africa
The effect it has on your family and on extended family and friends is huge.

Piece To Cam ERIN BATES: AT THE HEART OF THESE PERSONAL ACCOUNTS LIES A CRITICAL QUESTION - WHY DO SO MANY MIDDLE-AGED WOMEN IN SOUTH AFRICA DEVELOP MENINGIOMAS? AND IS SCIENCE FINALLY STARTING TO PROVIDE AN ANSWER?

(VO4) A DECADE AGO, NURSE CAROLINE MURRAY GOT A NASTY SURPRISE.
SHE DISCOVERED SHE’D BEEN LIVING WITH A BRAIN TUMOUR FOR SEVEN YEARS.
THE TUMOUR HAD A SPECIAL SCIENTIFIC NAME.
IT WAS CALLED A SPHENOID WING MENINGIOMA.

CAROLINE MURRAY
Meningioma Survivor, Fish Hoek
It’s in the sphenoid wing, which is a part of the brain. It's actually a sinus, so it's an opening, and the tumour forms within it. But my particular one just sort of really infiltrated into the base of the skull, which made it quite, quite difficult, and sort of surrounded the blood vessels and the nerves, and that's what made the surgery so complex.

(VO5) CAROLINE’S FIRST OPERATION WAS OPEN BRAIN SURGERY TO CUT THE TUMOUR OUT, BIT BY BIT.
BUT THE FOLLOWING OPERATIONS INVOLVED AN INNOVATIVE TECHNIQUE CALLED TRANS-ORBITAL SURGERY, PIONEERED IN SOUTH AFRICA BY EAR, NOSE AND THROAT SURGEON PROFESSOR DARLENE LUBBE.

PROF DARLENE LUBBE
Ear Nose Throat Surgeon, UCT
We were the first group in South Africa to do that, where we use the eye basically as a corridor to certain parts of the brain. And that's where we started doing these Sphenoid Wing Meningiomas for which we've become quite famous worldwide.

(VO6) WORKING WITH TINY CAMERAS AND PENETRATING THE SKULL THROUGH THE EYE AND NOSE MADE FOR A MORE SUCCESSFUL OUTCOME.
THIS IS NECESSARY BECAUSE THIS TYPE OF TUMOUR TYPICALLY WRAPS ITSELF AROUND THE NERVES, FIBRES AND ARTERIES OF THE BRAIN.
SURGEONS CALL THIS AREA “TIGER TERRITORY” BECAUSE IT IS SO EASY FOR SOMETHING TO GO WRONG.
AND ONLY A FEW IN SOUTH AFRICA ARE WILLING TO WORK ON SPHENOID WING MENINGIOMAS.

Piece To Cam ERIN BATES: IN SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE, MENINGIOMAS ARE CALLED BENIGN, AS THEY ARE NOT CANCEROUS.
BUT THEY ARE FAR FROM HARMLESS.

PROF DARLENE LUBBE
Ear Nose Throat Surgeon, UCT
The meningioma starts as a very small little area but as it grows in the space it really then starts invading and it will grow into this bone. So if I had to look at the skull from the front and that is what Trans-Orbital Surgery does, the neurosurgeons come in from the side, we come from the eye, so we don’t take out the eye out, but just to give you an impression of what you see, so you look at the skull and you gonna see that tumour.

(VO7) NEUROSURGEON DR BYRON DE JOHN IS PART OF THIS MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM.
THEY WORK ON PATIENTS SIMULTANEOUSLY TO SAVE TIME IN THEATRE.
THEY CAN RELIEVE PRESSURE INSIDE THE SKULL BUT SELDOM GET THE ENTIRE TUMOUR OUT.

DR BYRON DE JOHN
Neurosurgeon, UCT
We try and prioritize patients based on their disability level. So those that are losing vision we try prioritize. And those with very large tumours, those tumours having a lot of mass effect, you can see the raised intracranial pressure, will try and intervene early, and then prioritizing patients based on how long they've been waiting on our waiting lists.

(VO8) SOME OF THE WORK THEY DO IS CALLED DEBULKING - WHICH IS SCRAPING OUT TUMOUR MATTER TO RELIEVE THE PRESSURE BEHIND THE EYE.

PROF DARLENE LUBBE
Ear Nose Throat Surgeon
So the eyes get pushed forward, then they get referred to the hospital, and that's the only time they get referred or they say, I'm blind in the one eye, or the eye becomes disfigured. That's how they usually present.

(VO9) AT INTERNATIONAL MEETINGS, PROFESSOR LUBBE DISCOVERED THAT SHE WAS SEEING MANY MORE OF THESE CASES THAN SURGEONS FROM OTHER COUNTRIES.
AND THE MORE SHE OPERATED, THE LONGER HER WAITING LIST BECAME.
NINETY-NINE PER CENT OF THE PATIENTS WERE WOMEN - AND THERE WAS NO CLEAR REASON WHY….

PROF DARLENE LUBBE
Ear Nose Throat Surgeon
We have enough meningiomas waiting to be operated on to fill the next two years on a weekly basis. In fact, one of the private hospitals has donated some money in order for us to try and catch up, but one of these cases takes eight hours. So we try and do these cases as an extra on a Friday, but there's no way for us to catch up.

(VO10) FRENCH NEUROSURGEON, PROFESSOR SEBASTIEN FROELICH FINDS THIS UNUSUAL.
SPEAKING TO US FROM THE LARIBOISIÈRE HOSPITAL IN PARIS, HE SAYS HE SELDOM OPERATES ON THESE MENINGIOMAS IN FRANCE.

PROFESSOR SEBASTIEN FROELICH (accent on first e)
Specialist Neurosurgeon, Lariboisière Hospital
I have this feeling. I cannot prove it, I have the feeling that there is an abnormal number of Sphenoid Orbital Meningioma in South Africa. I may be wrong, but Darlene has a quite a high number of those patients, and this seems to me weird.

(VO11) FOR ALMOST TEN YEARS, FRENCH SCIENTISTS HAVE BEEN INVESTIGATING WHETHER THERE IS AN ASSOCIATION BETWEEN HORMONE DRUGS AND BRAIN TUMOURS.
AFTER SURVEYING 18000 WOMEN WITH MENINGIOMAS IN FRANCE, THIS HIGH-POWERED TEAM PUBLISHED A STUDY - WITH A STARTLING OUTCOME.

PROFESSOR SEBASTIEN FROELICH (accent on first e)
Specialist Neurosurgeon, Lariboisière Hospital
So the purpose of this study was to try to assess the risk of meningioma with some progestogen drugs, and especially with some drugs that we didn't studied until until now. And one of these drug is medroxyprogesterone.
Well, the t report confirmed that there is an increased risk of meningioma with medroxyprogesterone,I am sorry I forgot the abbreviation.

Piece To Cam ERIN BATES: IT IS A MOUTHFUL TO PRONOUNCE: MEDROXYPROGESTERONE ACETATE.
OR MORE SIMPLY MPA.
THIS IS THE SYNTHETIC FORM OF THE HORMONE PROGESTERONE.

(VO12) AND MPA IS THE KEY INGREDIENT OF A WIDELY USED CONTRACEPTIVE INJECTION IN SOUTH AFRICA CALLED DEPO-PROVERA.

SO THIS STUDY COULD HOLD THE KEY TO UNDERSTANDING WHY SO MANY SOUTH AFRICAN WOMEN WITH MENINGIOMAS END UP ON PROFESSOR LUBBE’S OPERATING TABLE.

PROF DARLENE LUBBE
Ear Nose Throat Surgeon, UCT
There's a huge bell going off, because we know that there is a risk with progesterone. We need to know: is there an increased risk with the progesterones that we use in South Africa? Is that the reason why we seeing more meningiomas? Is it anecdotal that we're seeing it because we haven't done the research. We've we're looking at retrospective studies and prospective studies, but we still need to do those to prove it.
.
(VO13) IN OTHER WORDS, THEY NEED TO FIND OUT MORE ABOUT THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN MPA AND BRAIN TUMOURS. SO PROFESSOR LUBBE STARTED TO PHONE HER PATIENTS ONE BY ONE TO ASK IF THEY HAD EVER BEEN ON THIS HIGH-DOSE CONTRACEPTIVE, WHICH IS ROUTINELY OFFERED TO WOMEN IN LOW-INCOME COUNTRIES.

(VO14) ONE OF THESE WAS CAROLINE FROM FISHOEK IN CAPE TOWN WHO HAD BEEN PRESCRIBED THE INJECTION AS A YOUNG WOMAN TO ADDRESS ENDOMETRIOSIS, A PAINFUL CONDITION OF THE UTERUS.

CAROLINE MURRAY
Meningioma Survivor, Fish Hoek
It made perfect sense. The fact that I'd been on Depo for 30 years, so when this came up I thought OK, Finally, something, you know, the penny dropped. This, this seems to me to be the reason. I'm sure this had something to do with Depo.

ERIN BATES: Were you cautioned about any potential side effects or counselled on any options?

CAROLINE MURRAY
Meningioma Survivor, Fish Hoek
I honestly don’t remember, it was so long ago. But I’m sure that gynae was very thorough and I am sure he gave me the best treatment that he knew possible at that time.

(VO15) THE DEPO-PROVERA SAFETY PAMPHLET HIGHLIGHTS A DANGER OF OSTEOPOROSIS. BUT IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT MENINGIOMAS. IT ALSO WARNS PATIENTS NOT TO USE IT FOR LONGER THAN TWO YEARS.

DEPO-PROVERA WAS LICENSED IN SOUTH AFRICA IN THE EARLY 1970S, CHIEFLY AS A CONTRACEPTIVE INJECTION FOR WOMEN AND TEENAGE GIRLS AS YOUNG AS THE AGE OF TWELVE.
KNOWN AS THE JAB OR SHOT, THIS HIGH DOSE CONTRACEPTIVE STOPS OVULATION FOR THREE MONTHS AT A TIME WITH OTHER BENEFITS FOR REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH.

Piece To Cam ERIN BATES:
SOUTH AFRICA IS ONE OF THE BIGGEST USERS OF THE THREE MONTH CONTRACEPTION INJECTION GLOBALLY.
IT’S CHEAP, IT’S DISCREET AND IT’S EASY TO DISTRIBUTE.

(VO16) IN OTTERY, OUTSIDE CAPE TOWN, SIXTY YEAR OLD WASELA ROSS IS ANOTHER ONE OF PROFESSOR LUBBE’S PATIENTS.

WASELA WAS ON DEPO FOR 29 YEARS BECAUSE THE NURSES AT THE CLINIC SAID IT WOULD BE GOOD FOR HER HEALTH.

UPSOUND WASELA ROSS: Hi, please come in.

UPSOUND ERIN BATES: Thank you so much.

UPSOUND WASELA ROSS: So nice to meet you.

UPSOUND ERIN BATES: It’s lovely to meet you as well.

ERIN BATES: So they told you about the benefits of the injection.

WASELA ROSS UPSOUND: Of the injection, yes.

ERIN BATES: for you, with the high blood pressure and even with, you know, diminishing some of the symptoms of menopause…

WASELA ROSS UPSOUND: Of Menopause.

ERIN BATES: Did they tell you of any of the risks it might have?

WASELA ROSS UPSOUND: Nope.

WASELA ROSS
Pensioner
It was just: Do you want more babies, huh? Now, take your injection and go, that's it.

(VO17) WHEN WASELA WAS DIAGNOSED WITH A MENINGIOMA TEN YEARS AGO SHE HAD NO IDEA WHAT CAUSED IT.
DESPITE THE OPERATION BRINGING SOME RELIEF, SHE SAYS HER LIFE WILL NEVER BE THE SAME AGAIN.

WASELA ROSS
Meningioma Survivor, Ottery
Whatever I breathe or smell or anything, there's no blockage here to control it like normal people. This one will go straight to my head, then I can feel it here, the smell, and then it comes back into the hollowness of where my eye is. And then the eye starts watering and it puffs.

(VO18) FOR A LONG TIME, WASELA FELT ISOLATED IN THIS ORDEAL.
BUT NOW SHE KNOWS SHE’S NOT ALONE.
THERE ARE OTHER WOMEN WHO WERE ON DEPO FOR DECADES WHO DISCOVERED MASSIVE TUMOURS IN THEIR HEADS.
AND THEY’RE IN TOUCH ONLINE.

JOANITA BARKHUIZEN
Meningioma Survivor, East London
It’s actually in the optic bone, as well as my skull’s bone, and in there’s in the soft tissue as well.

NICOLE LLOYD
Meningioma Survivor, Jeffrey’s Bay
Between blindness and paralyzing me and killing me, they had to leave some behind.

The true horror of sphenoid wing meningiomas appears to be only fully grasped by the people who have them growing inside their skulls, and the surgeons who try to help them. These invasive tumours often grow undetected for years, causing huge damage to the eyes and brain. In an investigation spanning two continents, Carte Blanche meets some of the meningioma patients who have had to undergo complex brain surgery to save their lives. Not only do they share this grisly experience, but they’ve also discovered that they were all on one of the world’s most widely available contraceptive injections - Depo-Provera - for decades. Now, new scientific evidence is suggesting a possible link between medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) - the synthetic hormone in Depo-Provera - and the development of brain tumours. Lawyers are preparing cases against the manufacturers of the so-called “jab” in several countries, including South Africa, after nine women with meningiomas approached them to consider action. Responding to growing pressure on this issue, the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) has recently recommended updating safety warnings about MPA-containing products to include the potential risk of meningioma. But for the women we have spoken to, this comes too little too late. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We show how standard government-issue contraception may need to be rethought following a BMJ study published last year
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have access to individuals in the medical world who are reacting to new information in the way of a study which may change the approach to a contraceptive drug globally, in particular in low income countries. The studies highlight a possible link between the three month injection Depo-Provera, which is made of the synthetic hormone, MPA, and devastating brain tumours. This new information, while not conclusive, could have direct impact on the lives of millions of women who rely on discreet contraception to manage family planning in poorer settings. The case studies we interviewed who were suffering from meningiomas and had been on Depo-Provera for a length of time - sometimes decades - are sufficiently angry to start planning for a class action against the manufacturer of the drug, Pfizer. Their health, independence and livelihoods have been severely impacted by the Meningiomas and they are angry about the suffering they have experienced. This association has direct consequences for contraception across the developing world.

metadata.Reason for legal: There is an accusation against a global pharmaceutical company that a drug they manufacture could have adverse side effects, which would make them and other organisations and governments liable for damages from women who suffer from meningiomas. As there are court cases being prepared in South Africa and other countries it would seem prudent to check for legal issues.
